default.py:66 normalizes with (standing_instructions or "").strip() or None, so None, "" and any str.strip()-empty value become None. Python's str.strip removes all Unicode whitespace, including the non-breaking space U+00A0 (the hint's first counterexample), so that input adds nothing. Zero-width space U+200B is Unicode category Cf, not whitespace, so it is not 'whitespace-only' text and falls outside the docstring's wording. With None, both branches are unchanged: the base_prompt branch returns base_prompt as-is (lines 113-115), and the default branch skips the ambiguity rule (lines 146-150, an empty list is spliced in at line 180) and the closing section (line 337). The built prompt is therefore the same as the unconfigured builder's. Absolute-claim trace: input '\u00a0 \n\t' -> None -> no section, no extra rule.
